# Finding ∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Setting Up Integration by Parts

I need to compute ∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx. Let me first find I = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx, then multiply by 2.

**First integration by parts:** Let u = cos(x), dv = exp(x)*dx

Then du = -sin(x)*dx, v = exp(x)

$$I = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \int \exp(x)\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** on ∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx: Let u = sin(x), dv = exp(x)*dx

Then du = cos(x)*dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \exp(x)\sin(x)\, dx = \exp(x)\sin(x) - \int \exp(x)\cos(x)\, dx = \exp(x)\sin(x) - I$$

## Solving for I

Substituting back:

$$I = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \exp(x)\sin(x) - I$$

$$2I = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \exp(x)\sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\exp(x)(\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2}$$

## Final Result

Multiplying by 2:

$$\int 2\exp(x)\cos(x)\, dx = \exp(x)(\cos(x) + \sin(x)) + C$$

## Verification

$$\frac{d}{dx}[\exp(x)(\sin(x) + \cos(x))] = \exp(x)(\sin(x) + \cos(x)) + \exp(x)(\cos(x) - \sin(x)) = 2*\exp(x)*\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x)) + C</answer>
